description:
The speed readout on the /fly HUD displays 'NaN km/s' for the entire duration of outer-planet missions (Galileo, Voyager 2, New Horizons, Dawn, Cassini). The readout is produced by passing the spacecraft's heliocentric distance (scR) and a hardcoded Earth→Mars Hohmann semi-major axis (1.262 AU) to vis-viva. For outer planets scR reaches 5–40 AU, far exceeding 2 × 1.262 AU, causing the vis-viva radicand (2/r − 1/a) to go negative and return NaN. The velocity-arrow visual indicator also uses this value and becomes zero-length or invisible as a secondary consequence.

Expected: The HUD speed readout shows a finite, physically meaningful numeric speed value (in km/s) at every point along any mission trajectory — computed from the vis-viva equation when the radicand is non-negative, and falling back to the local circular orbital speed when the radicand would be negative. The value should transition smoothly as the spacecraft moves through the solar system, never producing NaN.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulating any outer-planet mission (Galileo, Voyager 2, New Horizons, Dawn, Cassini) on /fly, the HUD speed readout shows a finite numeric string — not 'NaN' — at every timestep from departure through arrival. [code-invariant: NaN in a user-facing numeric readout is a self-evident bug. The reporter states 'the HUD speed readout just says NaN km/s the whole way. Looks completely broken.']
- When the vis-viva radicand (2/r − 1/a) is negative, the computed speed equals sqrt(µ_sun / r) — the local circular orbital speed at the spacecraft's heliocentric distance — not escape speed, not apohelion-clamped last-valid value, not hidden. This fallback is applied regardless of which SMA is passed; it is the function's defense against its own input regime. [reporter: Maintainer's explicit design decision: 'Option (a): fall back to the local circular orbital speed at that radius (sqrt(mu / r)). This is my explicit design decision as maintainer — not extrapolation, not clamping to the apohelion speed, not hiding the readout.']

Domain facts:
- The vis-viva equation v = sqrt(µ(2/r − 1/a)) requires the radicand to be non-negative. When r > 2a, (2/r − 1/a) < 0 and sqrt returns NaN.
- Outer-planet orbital radii (AU), from static/data/planets.json via lambert-grid.constants.ts: Jupiter ~5.20, Saturn ~9.54, Uranus ~19.19, Neptune ~30.07, Pluto ~39.48.
- The heliocentricSpeed function in fly-physics.ts:39-41 currently does pure vis-viva with no fallback — the fix point for the fallback branch.
- The DESTINATIONS map (lambert-grid.constants.ts:131-144) contains destination orbital SMAs; the arc builder (mission-arc.ts:169) computes per-mission transfer SMA as (r1+r2)/2 from live endpoints, but buildArcs does not return this value — it only returns point arrays.
